focus.name: terrain-handler-action-identities
focus.purpose: Promote the confirmed terrain-response handlers whose exact bodies identify a concrete player, surface-mode, or terrain-state action rather than a generic Block label.

targets.name: TerrainHandler_ApplySurfaceInteraction
targets.contract: Gate the surface interaction using player state and terrain flags, then publish PLAYER_WORLD_X/Y into the active interaction record when accepted.

targets.name: TerrainHandler_ApplyLandingResponse
targets.contract: Apply the landing vertical response, clear the horizontal response accumulator, arm grounded state, and refresh the player animation state.

targets.name: TerrainHandler_PushPlayerLeft
targets.contract: Move PLAYER_X left by eight pixels and clear the horizontal response accumulator.

targets.name: TerrainHandler_SetSurfaceMode
targets.contract: Set the surface-mode word at 0x00FFF0A4 to one.

targets.name: TerrainHandler_SetTerrainState
targets.contract: Set TERRAIN_STATE at 0x00FFF0D6, with the existing scene-state-5 special branch preserved.

targets.name: TerrainHandler_StopAndAlignPlayer
targets.contract: Stop player velocities, clear the response accumulator, and align player coordinates and animation state when terrain blocks movement.

targets.name: TerrainHandler_LaunchPlayer
targets.contract: Set PLAYER_VY=-0x0500 and PLAYER_VX=-0x0400, select the terrain-launch animation, and arm the airborne state.

targets.name: TerrainHandler_SnapPlayerToGrid
targets.contract: Snap PLAYER_X/PLAYER_Y to the 16-pixel terrain grid, clear response state, select the alignment animation, and arm its short timer.

targets.name: TerrainHandler_BouncePlayer
targets.contract: Set PLAYER_VX=-0x0400 and PLAYER_VY=0x0200, select the bounce animation, and retain the existing event-queue side effect.

contracts: All targets are unique fixed-ROM functions selected from TERRAIN_RESPONSE_HANDLER_TABLE at 0x004554.
The canonical names describe exact direct effects established by the 68000 bodies and existing terrain dispatch evidence.
Every prior name remains an explicit compatibility alias; no function range or behavior assignment changes.
evidence: existing Level 01 terrain and player-response runtime findings
limitations: The names identify direct handler actions and do not claim that each behavior is active in every level or route.
Indirect selector reachability remains governed by the existing whole-ROM dispatch evidence.
